title: Utah: obtain the franchise notice receipt before a covered offer
description: Calendar the receipt, annual renewal and information updates using the current 2026 statute.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The receipt is a pre-offer dependency
paragraphs: Utah §13-15-201(2) requires proof of notice receipt before a person offers or sells a franchise to be located in Utah or to a Utah resident. The filing states substantial compliance with the federal Franchise Rule and includes required applicant, brand, address and identification details. Preparing an FDD does not itself produce this receipt.

sections.heading: Use the current renewal and update calendar
paragraphs: The current section, amended effective May 6, 2026, makes the receipt valid for one year from issue. Renewal compliance is due at least 30 days before expiry. Filing information that becomes incorrect or incomplete must be updated within 30 days. Preserve the issued receipt, the preparation deadline and the change record.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a UK technical-services network
paragraphs: A brand plans a Utah-resident prospect campaign while its company secretary changes the selling entity’s principal address. The team must manage both the pre-offer receipt and the information update. An internal checkbox that a filing was prepared is not evidence that the required receipt was obtained.

sections.heading: Notice and disclosure filing are different routes
paragraphs: The Act separates the qualifying franchise notice path from the general business-opportunity disclosure filing path. Section 201(2)(c) routes those who do not qualify for the notice path to subsection (1). The latter has its own content and ten-business-day purchaser-disclosure provisions. Neither receipt is state approval. Applicable federal FDD delivery remains an independent task.

sections.heading: Identify the protected relationship
paragraphs: Vermont Title 9, Chapter 107 covers defined equipment and machinery dealerships. Its dealer agreement can be oral or written, but the dealer and inventory definitions matter. Heavy construction equipment and a specified single-line dealer category are excluded. A pure service franchise should not be treated as covered merely because it uses a trademark.

sections.heading: Fictional example: services plus utility equipment

sections.heading: Different events use different timelines
paragraphs: Section 4072 generally requires cause, 120 days’ notice and a 60-day cure opportunity. Market-penetration termination has a separate 24-month initial process and a final notice period; specified events permit immediate termination. Sections 4073–4074 address conditional repurchase with request, eligibility, valuation and payment requirements. Do not extract one deadline and apply it to every exit.

sections.heading: The definitions reach beyond farm machinery

Those conditions are part of coverage. A brand license or service contract alone does not establish that the Act applies.

sections.heading: Fictional example: equipment and repair rights

sections.heading: Notice and repurchase are separate duties

Track the termination date, physical return and payment separately; do not call the whole stock balance automatically recoverable.

sections.heading: Separate equipment distribution from service delivery

sections.heading: Fictional example: a grounds-care network

sections.heading: One notice period does not cover every dealer
paragraphs: The general §§115/117 regime ordinarily uses 180 days’ notice with 60 days to cure; the single-line §116 regime ordinarily uses 90 days with 60 days to cure. These are conditional sector rules, not a general right to terminate any franchise on notice.
